subject.title: [Bug]: Concurrent allow-always approvals silently lose allowlist entries (last-write-wins race in exec-approvals.json)

question: Should maintainers adopt and complete the existing guarded exec-approvals write path, replace it with a narrower core persistence fix, or defer this to a broader runtime-tracking redesign?
rationale: The affected file controls command-execution approval policy, and choosing the permanent write consistency contract affects gateway, node-host, admin policy writes, and availability behavior.

options.title: Adopt the guarded write contract
options.body: Refresh or replace the open stale-write fix so all allow-always and usage writes re-read/merge under the same lock or freshness guard before merge.

options.title: Narrow to this allow-always race
options.body: Land a smaller fix for concurrent allow-always entries now, while keeping node metadata/admin revocation hardening in the separate open security issue.

options.title: Defer to runtime-state redesign
options.body: Keep this open behind the broader runtime-tracking separation work if maintainers want to remove mutable metadata from `exec-approvals.json` instead of hardening the current file store first.

recommendation.title: Adopt the guarded write contract
recommendation.body: Refresh or replace the open stale-write fix so all allow-always and usage writes re-read/merge under the same lock or freshness guard before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent commits and the related maintainer draft make vincentkoc the best current routing candidate for the exec approvals persistence direction.
